plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because if you win, you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid), so bidding your true value ensures you win exactly when the item is worth more to you than the price you'd pay, and lose otherwise - maximizing expected profit. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $39.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With a private value of $27, bidding exactly $27 maximizes expected profit by ensuring I win whenever profitable and never overpay.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with 3 bidders. In second-price auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own), so overbidding risks negative profit, and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $13, I should bid exactly $13 to ensure I only win when profitable and capture maximum surplus when I do.
